subject: Information Theory
title: Why Secrets Need Math
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Why Secrets Need Math.

hook.text: Julius Caesar shifted each letter three places to hide his orders. It fooled centurions but not mathematicians.

buildup.text: For centuries, secrecy relied on clever tricks. Frequency analysis cracked almost every classical cipher.

discovery.text: Shannon proved in 1949 that truly unbreakable encryption exists, but only under strict conditions.

twist.text: Security isn't about hiding methods. It's about making the math so hard that breaking it takes centuries.

climax.text: Modern cryptography assumes the enemy knows the system. Only the key is secret.

punchline.text: Hide the key, not the method.

quiz.question: What did Shannon prove about encryption?
options: Truly unbreakable encryption exists under strict conditions
